# Best open-ear earbuds for running

Open-ear models let you hear traffic and other runners. They don't guarantee safety, so keep the volume low enough to hear your surroundings. I can't browse, so I'm linking to the reviews, which carry the current buy links. Prices are as listed in them and may have changed.

**Top picks**

- **Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (about $199, down from $299).** Runner's World named these best overall. They have a comfortable clip design, good sound, and physical buttons that are easier to use mid-run. Downsides are IPX4 water resistance, about 7 hours per charge, and slightly quiet volume in loud traffic. Runner's World also says Bose plans new open-ear earbuds within a month, so you may want to wait. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) | [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Best for long runs and rain: Shokz OpenDots 2 ($200).** They last 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and are rated IP57. WIRED's top pick, and the clip leaves the top of your ear free for hats and glasses. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 ($180 list, about $125 at some retailers).** It's the most open option, with 12 hours of battery and physical buttons. WIRED rated it 8/10. The neckband can interfere with long hair and winter hats. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/) | [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- **Best for strong bass: Nothing Ear (Open) (about $99 at Amazon, $149 list).** SoundGuys picked it as best overall and best for running. It has IP54 resistance, a parametric EQ, and good bass for this category. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Budget picks**

- **Anker Soundcore AeroFit 2.** It's IP55 with a 10-hour battery and an ear-hook design. SoundGuys lists it at $79.99 at Amazon, while a Dealectric deal page lists $129.99, or $104 with code AFSC20. Those prices differ a lot, so compare before buying. The Dealectric link is an affiliate link and opens Soundcore's store. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/) | [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2)
- **JLab Flex Open (about $40–50).** A low-risk way to test whether clip-ons suit you. Sound is less detailed than pricier pairs. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- **Soundpeats PearlClip Pro ($50).** WIRED's cheap pick, also a clip-on. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Quick guidance**

- Want the most awareness and heavy bass: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2.
- Want the best sound in a clip-on: Bose Ultra Open.
- Run in rain or go for very long runs: Shokz OpenDots 2.
- Unsure about open-ear: start with the JLab or Soundpeats.

If you tell me your budget, phone (iPhone or Android), and whether you wear hats, glasses, or have long hair, I can narrow it to one.
